chapter: Opening and the New York trip
title: Nickname origin in New York and leaving New Orleans in 1912
summary: Musicians in New York teased him as 'Montutti' when Johnny Dodds ran late; he places it before World War I and says he left home in 1912.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Holler at each other, you know. He might do something. Johnny Dotslider would come in a little late or something, and... They'd come on there, you look like old Montutti. What band was that? Kid Horry. Kid Horry, huh? In New York? When was he in New York with Johnny Dots? Johnny Dots was in New York with us. When was that? What year was that? That was... I was, uh...
Let's see how it... Was that before the war or after World War I?
That was, uh... Before the war or after World War I?
That was, uh... Four o'clock. Yeah. I was...
I was, uh... I was, uh... Three o'clock.

Mm-hmm, when they had the big storm. Do you remember that big storm in September 1915?
